newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee reverses to end down.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee reverses to end down.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures tracked easier New York values and finished Thursday lower, erasing earlier gains on light trade selling, traders said.

As in New York, volume was extremely thin ahead of the long weekend in the United States. Traders also turned their attention to the more active cocoa which came under a heavy sell-off after the recent run-up.
Values were initially perked up by light manufacturer buying.
Overall volume stood at just 2,504 lots.
September traded between $1,855 and $1,780 to finish the day $55 down at $1,785. November also slipped $45 to $1,780.
The New York market is closed on Friday for the Independence Day holiday.
U.S. futures had been weighed down by easing fears of a damaging frost in Brazil this weekend.
Traders also cited the jump in coffee pending grading on the exchange. More than 40,000 60-kg bags of coffee are awaiting grading in exchange-certified warehouses.

"On the negative side is the jump in coffee potentially available on the CSCE (the New York market), almost enough to wipe out the remnants of the open interest, and certainly enough to push prices," broker GNI said in a commentary.

U.S. forecaster Weather Services Corp said cold air building over Argentina on Friday was expected to pass off to the south of Brazil's coffee belt as the warm, high pressure dominating the area continued its hold over the region.
